mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative over a 60-day horizon following a GDP increase.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 9% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business confidence may decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 20-day horizon following a significant rise in unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases but unemployment (UNRATE) also rises, it may indicate structural imbalances in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 20-day horizon despite conflicting labor market signals.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may indicate a tight monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and thus negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 60-day horizon with high federal funds rates.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) may lead to inflationary pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns as higher costs erode profit margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 20-day horizon despite rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 60-day horizon following a decline in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) remains high, it may indicate inefficiencies in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 60-day horizon despite conflicting economic signals.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in housing starts (HOUST) may indicate reduced consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over a 60-day horizon despite slowing housing starts.
